reason: The cited evidence does not address multilayer interfaces or their effect on creep. E1 discusses dislocation behavior in a single-phase refractory HEA, E2 describes stress-dependent creep mechanisms in monolithic HEAs, and E3 reviews nanoindentation creep testing methods. None provide support for the key premises about interface barriers, diffusion impedance, or comparative creep resistance.
premises: Multilayer interfaces block dislocation motion (including climb) across layers
Multilayer interfaces impede atomic diffusion (sluggish diffusion effect)
Blocking dislocations and diffusion reduces steady-state creep strain rate
The effects are synergistic and increase effective activation energy for creep
Monolithic HEA coatings lack these interface-mediated barriers
